root_idea.summary: A central image of the root is the easy, abundant flowing of a substance.
root_idea.development: From physical flow and overflow, the lexicon develops causative uses for pouring and filling, movement in a mass like a flood, extended discourse, abundance, and related figurative expressions.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized Form I citation form فَاضَ.
Displayed under the normalized Form IV citation form أَفَاضَ.

senses.definition: To flow, run, or overflow from fullness; of water and other fluids, including tears.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, the form describes eyes overflowing or flowing with tears.

senses.definition: To pour out or forth water, tears, or another fluid.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quran uses this causative construction for pouring water upon or toward someone; the broader lexical construction also applies to tears and other fluids.

senses.definition: To move on, press forward, or depart in a group.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic expression أَفَضْتُمْ مِنْ عَرَفَاتٍ and related wording describe the collective departure or onward movement from ʿArafāt after gathering.

senses.definition: To enter into, launch into, or engage in discourse.
senses.usage_conditions: With فِي, the construction denotes entering into or proceeding in speech; Quranic contexts include discussing or indulging in a matter.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become abundant, numerous, or plentiful; of good, wealth, or other things, to abound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of physical overflowing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A report or story spread abroad among people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative use likening the circulation of news to flowing water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place became wide or ample.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Figurative usage applied to a place or expanse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A coat of mail spread over or covered someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction describing the garment as spreading over its wearer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To die; for the soul to depart.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This usage is dialectally and lexicographically disputed, with some authorities preferring فَاظَ; it is nevertheless attested as a Classical usage for فَاضَ, especially with نَفْسٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For the bosom to overflow with anger or another strong emotion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative construction with the overflowing substance understood as an emotion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a full bosom to disclose or let out a secret that it can no longer conceal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction فَاضَ صَدْرُهُ بِالسِّرِّ describes disclosure caused by inward fullness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A divine suggestion or an insinuation, including what the Devil casts into the mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended, figurative use of flowing or being imparted.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To fill a vessel so that it overflows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This causative construction may also be used in the less specific sense of filling a vessel, though overflowing is identified as the preferable interpretation in the cited discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause good, wealth, or another benefit to abound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative causative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a coat of mail on someone, as though pouring or spreading it over him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative transitive construction with عَلَيْهِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The circumambulation of the Kaʿbah performed on returning from Minā to Mecca; the circumambulation of visitation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional pilgrimage term derived from the movement or return denoted by إِفَاضَةٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impel or urge a riding animal to run quickly; to make a camel exert itself in a fast run.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized equestrian use; إِفَاضَةٌ can also denote a push or drive onward.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To enter upon or begin an action or employment and proceed in it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended construction distinct from the Quranic discourse use, applied to an activity or undertaking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To impel, thrust, cast, or throw a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A transitive construction with بِالشَّيْءِ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a camel to propel its cud from the stomach and expel it, sometimes in a scattered and copious manner.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The specialized expression أَفَاضَ البَعِيرُ بِجِرَّتِهِ may also refer to the audible sound of chewing and cud.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Not to make a word or sentence clear, distinct, or perspicuous.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression مَا أَفَاضَ بِكَلِمَةٍ is an idiomatic negative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To handle, shuffle, deal out, or distribute gaming arrows.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized figurative use with the gaming arrows, القِدَاح.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put or mix a thing among one's property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is reported for a transmitted wording whose reading is itself noted as possibly erroneous.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For a woman to become wide or large in the belly and flabby in flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source explicitly applies this passive construction to a woman; it is a specialized bodily description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cause the vaginal and rectal passages of a woman to become joined in the context of devirginization.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare anatomical usage identified as equivalent to أَفْضَى, with the two forms related by transposition in the cited explanation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To flow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare attestation of the Form V verb; the source itself notes that it is not otherwise readily found.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To ask for the pouring out of water or another fluid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An inchoative/requesting use of the Form X verb.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For news or a story to spread widely; of a valley, to become broad and abundant in trees.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The news usage is an extended sense of spreading; the valley usage combines breadth with abundance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A river or abundant, overflowing body of water; also a named great river such as the Nile or the river of Basrah.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural forms show that this is a substantive noun rather than merely a verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A horse that runs much, swiftly, or vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative description likening the horse's speed to pouring water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who is bountiful, munificent, or abundant in beneficence.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative personal attribute derived from abundance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Muchness, abundance, or a large quantity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This includes the expression غَيْضًا مِنْ فَيْضٍ, meaning a little from much.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A large gift, or a gift, favor, or grace.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended substantive use; the plural فُيُوضٌ is reported.

other_classical_meanings.definition: By way of instinct; instinctively.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A fixed figurative phrase derived from the sense of an imparted or flowing influence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Death.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A rare substantive use explained as the outpouring of the soul.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The corpse and bier carried in a funeral procession.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In the expression ذَهَبْنَا فِي فَيْضِ فُلَانٍ, the noun refers metonymically to the deceased and funeral procession.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A river containing much water or flowing abundantly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intensive adjective applied to a river.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A full watering-trough, sea, or great river that overflows or pours vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participial adjective describing abundant or overflowing water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Discourse into which people have entered, launched, or proceeded at length.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The phrase describes discourse in which speakers have pushed on, dilated, or begun to engage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A wide or ample coat of mail.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of armor spread over its wearer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wide or full in the belly; of a woman, large-bellied and flabby in flesh.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source applies the masculine form to a man and the feminine form to a woman; some descriptions add unusual height or bodily fullness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the vaginal and rectal passages joined.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized interpretation reported by some authorities and connected with مُفْضَاةٌ by transposition.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who asks for the pouring out of water or another fluid.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An active participle of the requesting use of اِسْتَفَاضَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A story or piece of news that has spread among people.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction مُسْتَفِيضٌ فِيهِ is also reported; the bare form مُسْتَفَاضٌ in this sense is rejected by many lexicographers, though some usage is recorded.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Discourse that has been entered into, begun, or proceeded in.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This passive construction is reported as an alternative usage, while the bare مُسْتَفَاضٌ is generally disallowed for this meaning.

cautions: Lane records substantial disagreement over whether فَاضَ and فَاضَتْ نَفْسُهُ may mean “died,” with some authorities preferring فَاظَ; the death usage is therefore kept as Classical evidence rather than assigned to a Quranic sense.

Several derived and participial entries involve rare, restricted, or disputed usage, especially the Form V flow verb, the property-mixing wording, and the bare form مُسْتَفَاضٌ; their conditions are stated with the relevant qualifications.
